issue: शङ्खनिनदम् कृत्वा — the first half has 11 mātrās against the 12 of the others; शङ्खनिनादं कृत्वा would fit the metre. निनद is a word too ("sound"), so the base stays. Only one witness.
हन्सावन ललिता — हन्स for हंस (swan) as the page types nasals; हंसावन ("swan-grove"?) or हंसावलि ("rows of swans") are possible readings. Only one witness.
our reading: The swans play gracefully (हन्सावन read as the swans' lovely play).
alternatives: हंसावलि ललिता (a lovely row of swans)

issue: रचयति कलाकलापं नृत्यति मुदसहिता: the feminine subject is not named; ललिता (the lovely one) is read as the subject.
our reading: The lovely one, full of joy, unfolds all her arts and dances.
alternatives: Gaurī (Lalitā) dances; a peahen spreads her tail (कलाप) and dances; ललिता qualifies the swans.

issue: The dancer of this stanza is not named; the ḍamaru makes it Śiva, though नूपुरमुज्ज्वलिता is feminine in form.
our reading: Śiva whirls and dances, plays the ḍamaru.
alternatives: Gaurī dances (anklets), Śiva plays the ḍamaru.

issue: रामस्त्रिजटानाथं: read रामः + त्रिजटानाथम् (त्रिजट, an epithet of Śiva, MW). Rāma may be Śrī Rāma or the poet naming himself; सन्गतिमेवं read as this song (सङ्गीतम्?) or सङ्गतिम्.
our reading: Rāma bows to the Lord of the matted locks; whoever recites this song daily…
alternatives: The poet Rāma (a signature); सङ्गतिम्, 'this union (of Śiva and Gaurī)'.
